body:
I resonate with Job. I feel like his friends response to his plights are very "Christian" in the modern sense, very apologetic. 

I feel vindicated reading Job's cry: 

> "Who does not know all these things? ... ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky and they will tell you; or speak to the earth and it will teach you or let the fish in the sea inform you. Which of these does not know that the hand of the lord has done this" (Job 12:73 12:7-9) 

In my own struggles with my faith I often find the responses of my fellow Christians to be inadequate and lacking empathy. My first instinct is to be angry. Angry because I feel patronized, that my fellow Christians are just spouting advice to signal their own virtue. 

But that is not the case. Really they are just trying to help, but I don't let them understand my situation. I've studied Christianity, I have a fair knowledge of apologetics. I am not arrogant enough to say that I am an expert or even an amateur, but the standard advice for struggling faith is something I've heard time and time again. 

I don't really know how to respond when people give me advice anymore. I don't want to stop talking about my struggles with faith but I don't want the advice that is offered to me. But these people were placed in my life by God to tell me something, show me something, even if it's not through the words they say. I must be thankful for that.
